source: a 3d dti but it's called fashion week and you wake up on a bed walk into your closet and pick an outfit a y2k, cute core, or emo or big puffy dresses and you have a 5 minute time limit and when the time is up you go on the runway and people around the world will vote you stars

answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the bedroom and runway read as glossy modern fashion-show, or bright stylized toon?
answers.answer: Use a bright stylized toon look that fits the cute Fashion Week dress-up vibe.

answers.ask: Is the bedroom and closet one shared dressing area everyone uses, or a private copy per player?
answers.answer: Give each player a private bedroom and closet so everyone can pick their outfit without crowding.

scene_prompt: Create a bright stylized-toon 3D fashion dress-up map with private bedroom-and-closet dressing suites for each player. Each suite begins at a bed and opens into a personal closet area displaying outfit options including Y2K, cute-core, emo, and large puffy dresses. Connect the dressing area to a glossy fashion-show runway, with a clear catwalk and viewing space arranged around it for spectators.
blob:
### Genre
Dominant genre: Roleplay & Avatar Sim, specifically a dress-up social experience. The timed outfit selection and audience voting establish the dress-up format, but those mechanics do not add layout components.

### Shape and preset
Use `stage-runway`, matching the Dress Up preset. Here it is a public glossy catwalk attached to player-specific preparation suites rather than a single shared backstage room. The preset’s runway-and-dressing-room form remains recognisable, while the requested private suites replace any communal preparation area.

### Config requirements
Use `building-interior` as visible geometry: each player has an enterable private bedroom suite containing its closet. Do not add unrequested town circulation, NPC crowds, photo vignettes, or generic social plazas. The spectator viewing space is physical runway-side architecture, not an ambient NPC population.

### Layout components
Build a repeated set of private bedroom-and-closet suites, one private copy per player. Each compact suite begins at a bed in the bedroom area and opens directly into a personal closet/display zone, with visibly separated outfit displays for Y2K, cute-core, emo, and large puffy dresses. A controlled exit from every suite feeds into the same public runway venue.

Make the runway the dominant central zone: a long, glossy catwalk with a presentation end, broad enough for a single avatar’s fashion walk and clearly visible from both sides. Arrange the spectator viewing area along the catwalk edges and at its presentation end, oriented toward the model path rather than toward the dressing suites. Keep suite doors and service connections behind or beside the runway so private preparation spaces do not visually clutter the fashion-show focal view. Use clean interior floors, rounded furniture, wardrobe racks, mirrors, pastel accent lighting, and a contained venue boundary. Frame the isometric composition with the runway diagonally prominent in the foreground and one representative open suite visible behind it, while implying the repeated private-suite system.

### Render order
Use `isometric`: render the isometric venue first as authoritative, then derive the top-down view. The public runway and repeated suites need a polished fashion-show composition, but invalid route topology would not make the experience unplayable.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale: medium, driven by the shared runway venue plus replicated per-player dressing-suite template. Theme: bright stylized toon, cute Fashion Week glamour, glossy pastel fashion-show interior. Pipeline modifiers: `P3`, because play crosses from private interior suites into the public runway venue; `P4`, because each player’s private bedroom-and-closet suite is a separate instanced space from the shared fashion-show map.
